        Before you read the tea leaves
        
      
    
        
    
        
      
        Killmails only tell half the story.
        
      
        Every number GoSleuth shows comes from killmails, and a killmail is only written when something dies. Nothing is recorded for the ships that warped off, the fights that ended with no losses, or the half of a battle on the other side of a gate or wormhole.
        
      
        That's survivorship bias turned inside out: you see only the losses, never the ones who got away. Some things never appear on a killmail at all:
        
      
          
        
        • Objectives. A fight that cost 3B ISK to save a 20B Keepstar looks like a loss.
          • 
        
        • Logistics. Logi pilots who kept everyone alive aren't listed, despite our requests.
          • 
        
        • Fights with no deaths. If nothing died, it never happened as far as the data knows.
          • 
      
        
      
        GoSleuth gathers what the killmails show and lays it out clearly. Interpreting it is up to you. Treat what you see as clues, not conclusions.

            The cache actions take effect straight away, without Save. Moving into a folder that already has a GoSleuth cache replaces it.
            

      
            Debugging
            
      
      
            Each search's log is saved as a zip of readable text files, the newest 10 kept. It includes the targets searched and your preferences, but not your user name, recent searches, holdings, or ignored allies. Crashes are always logged. Debug mode turns itself off when the app closes.

            Clear the cache?
            
      
            Anything cleared is looked up again from the ESI when next needed, so the next searches will be slower. This can not be undone.
            
      
            Most of the cache keeps itself fresh: pilots, corporations and alliances are looked up again after 24 hours, and ships, systems and other game data with each EVE data release. Killmails never change, so they are kept until cleared.
